result.note: Tested the concrete facts of the US waiver for Indian purchases of stranded Russian oil. Skipped the speculative talk of wider sanctions easing.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the United States granted India a waiver relating to Russian oil. Consider the following statements:
items: The waiver allowed India to buy Russian oil already stranded at sea for a period of 30 days.
The oil covered by the waiver was estimated to meet about a month of India's oil demand.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told G7 ministers that these cargoes would not benefit the Kremlin because the oil was already loaded.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Nomura estimated the 20-30 million barrels available would cover just four days of Indian demand, not a month. Bessent also said India would eventually buy more American crude instead, and the US signalled that any further easing would likely be just for India.
questions.source: Nomura analysts note the estimated 20-30 million barrels available cover just four days of Indian demand.
